mbot2.learn: Robotics, sensors, movement, problem solving, block-based coding and a path toward Python.
mbot2.fit: Learners who want a programmable robot with room to progress beyond first-step coding.
mbot2.why: Makeblock combines a physical aluminum robot, multiple sensors and a learning path from blocks to Python.
mbot2.consider: A higher-cost choice. Check device compatibility and current bundle contents before ordering.

elegoo.t: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit
elegoo.learn: Breadboarding, LEDs, sensors, modules, wiring and introductory microcontroller programming.
elegoo.fit: Teens and adults who want hands-on electronics rather than a finished toy.
elegoo.why: A substantial component set and structured tutorial path at an accessible entry price.
elegoo.consider: The official U.S. page was showing sold out when checked; availability can change.

botley.learn: Sequencing, logic, spatial reasoning, problem solving and early programming concepts.
botley.fit: Young learners and families who want coding play without a phone, tablet or app.
botley.why: Botley makes early coding tangible and screen-free while allowing increasingly long command sequences.
botley.consider: Requires 5 AAA batteries, not included. Contains small parts; follow manufacturer safety guidance.

buildbox.learn: Mechanisms, physics, iterative building, experimentation and engineering thinking.
buildbox.fit: Kids who enjoy guided hands-on engineering projects and recurring builds.
buildbox.why: The subscription format turns engineering into an ongoing activity rather than a single project.
buildbox.consider: Review current plan, renewal, shipping and cancellation terms before subscribing.

edison.learn: Sequencing, loops, functions, sensors, graphical coding and progression toward text-based programming.
edison.fit: Learners who want several coding approaches in one compact educational robot.
edison.why: Edison supports screen-free barcode/card coding, EdBlocks, EdScratch and EdPy.
edison.consider: USB programming support varies by device/browser; iPad uses screen flashing for supported environments.

hackpack.learn: Robotics, coding, mechanisms, experimentation and creative hardware hacking.
hackpack.fit: Teens and adults who want more sophisticated recurring robotics builds.
hackpack.why: It extends Electroys beyond children's products into hands-on projects for older learners and adults.
hackpack.consider: Review current subscription and device requirements before joining.

arduino.learn: Current, voltage, resistance, digital logic, circuits, programming and open-ended experimentation.
arduino.fit: Middle-school learners, homeschoolers and self-learners who want a structured Arduino introduction.
arduino.why: Arduino combines the UNO R3, breadboard, multimeter, sensors/actuators and guided online learning.
arduino.consider: Requires compatible computer/USB setup and Arduino IDE. Online content requires kit activation.

snap.learn: Working electrical circuits through projects such as radios, alarms, doorbells and electronic games.
snap.fit: Beginners who want hands-on electronics without soldering or breadboard wiring.
snap.why: Snap-together modules make circuit building approachable while demonstrating real electrical relationships.
snap.consider: Requires 4 AA batteries, not included. Verify current package contents and safety guidance.
